To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the two-particle azimuthal correlation function is not sensitive to the details of the initial energy density distribution, (ii) the two-particles correlation function is sensitive to the longitudinal profile of the initial energy, and (iii) the two-pair correlation function is sensitive only to the initial energy density profile.

(a) the two-particle energy density correlation function from the hydrodynamic fluctuations is negative at small azimuthal separation and positive at large separation; (b) the correlation function is sensitive to the magnitude of the radial flow and to the longitudinal extent of the fluctuations; (c) the correlation function from the hotspots has a similar shape to that of the hydrodynamic fluctuations, but with the sign reversed; (d) the two-particles correlation function from hotspots with the same longitudinal extent as
the correlations between particles emitted from different hotspots can be used to probe the hydrodynamic evolution of the medium created in heavy ion collisions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of hydrodynamics of the quark gluon plasma.
understanding how fluctuations of the initial state of heavy ion collisions affect final state observables.
the study of fluctuations in the initial conditions and the subsequent evolution of such fluctuations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the observed azimuthal anisotropies in the final state are a result of the initial state anisotropic distribution of the produced partons, which is in turn a consequence of the anisotropic initial energy density distribution.
the data are consistent with a hydrodynamic origin of the two-particles correlations.
the hydrodynamic model of fluctuations is not able to describe the two-particle azimuthal correlations observed experimentally.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hydrodynamic fluctuations can explain the observed long-range azimuthal correlations in heavy-ion collisions at RHIC and the large rapidity correlations in PbPb collisions at the LHC.

the two-particle correlations from the hotspots can be described by a simple model which includes radial flow, and the two-particle angular correlations are sensitive to the initial conditions of the hydrodynamic evolution.
hydrodynamic fluctuations and correlations are a natural and important part of the theory of the initial state.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hydrodynamic response to such localized perturbations is not a simple Gaussian distribution of the energy density fluctuations.
hydrodynamic fluctuations can produce a correlation signal which is qualitatively different from that of a single particle emission source.
the hydrodynamic fluctuations and correlations of the initial energy density are not the only source for two-particle correlation functions.
